united-states-postal-service.title: United States Postal Service
united-states-postal-service.body:
The United States Postal Service (USPS) is the federal agency responsible for mail delivery and, through its handling of mail ballots, a central actor in American election administration.[{n}]

## 2026 election order dispute

President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s executive order on election administration instructed the USPS to establish new standards for mail-in ballots, one of several provisions blocked in 23 Democrat-led states by a federal appeals court in July 2026.[{n}] Badlands commentary framed the resulting litigation as a conflict over decision rights: the plaintiff states sued on the theory that the administration cannot govern the Postal Service, yet states plainly have no authority over federal executive agencies either.[{n}] The Brief argued that if neither the states nor the President may direct the USPS, the question of who is constitutionally authorized to exercise its decision rights becomes unavoidable — and that clarifying such matters is important.[{n}]

department-of-homeland-security.title: Department of Homeland Security
department-of-homeland-security.body:
## Role in the 2026 election order

President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s executive order on election administration directed the Department of Homeland Security to compile lists of confirmed US citizens eligible to vote and provide them to the states, a citizenship-verification function at the heart of the order's proof-of-citizenship measures.[{n}] The provision was among those blocked in 23 Democrat-led states when a federal appeals court declined in July 2026 to lift Judge [[indira-talwani|Talwani]]'s injunction while litigation continues.[{n}]

department-of-justice.title: Department of Justice
department-of-justice.body:
## 2026 election order litigation

President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s executive order on election administration directed the Justice Department to prioritize investigations into state and local election officials who issue federal ballots to people deemed ineligible to vote.[{n}] The Department subsequently asked a federal appeals court to lift the injunction blocking key portions of the order in 23 Democrat-led states; the court denied that request in late July 2026, leaving Judge [[indira-talwani|Talwani]]'s injunction intact and setting up a likely [[supreme-court-of-the-united-states|Supreme Court]] fight over presidential authority in federal elections.[{n}]

benjamin-netanyahu.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
benjamin-netanyahu.body:
## Media campaign over Israel's reputation (July 2026)

A growing number of major media outlets argued in July 2026 that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has inflicted lasting damage on [[israel|Israel]]'s standing with the American public, contending that years of partisan political alignment, the ongoing Gaza war, and repeated clashes with US administrations eroded what was once broad bipartisan support.[{n}] Commentators argued Netanyahu had transformed Israel from a largely bipartisan issue into an increasingly polarizing one in American politics.[{n}] [[pew-research-center|Pew Research Center]] polling found unfavorable views of Israel and declining confidence in Netanyahu had risen since 2022, worsening across demographic groups and among younger voters in both major parties.[{n}]

The criticism coincided with renewed strains between Washington and Jerusalem: while President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] praised [[turkey|Turkey]] as a "tremendous ally," he also publicly criticized Israeli military operations during a meeting with Netanyahu, underscoring increasingly visible policy differences even as the alliance remained intact.[{n}]

[[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] identified a repeating pattern: the last time Netanyahu "tried to crash the White House," in September 2025 during the UN General Assembly, Trump responded by inviting [[recep-tayyip-erdogan|Erdogan]] to the White House the day before Netanyahu was scheduled to address the assembly; with Netanyahu again inviting himself, Trump was again using Erdogan to signal his real intent.[{n}] In that commentator's view, Trump's plan is not to wage kinetic war against Israel but to destroy its public reputation "by feeding into its greatest indulgences and allowing it the space to show the world what it truly is," with Israel's war against Iran costing it the goodwill accumulated over fifteen years.[{n}]

israel.title: Israel
israel.body:
## American public opinion (2026)

By July 2026 a growing number of major media outlets argued that Prime Minister [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]] had inflicted lasting damage on Israel's standing with the American public, citing years of partisan alignment, the ongoing Gaza war, and repeated clashes with US administrations as having eroded once-broad bipartisan support.[{n}] [[pew-research-center|Pew Research Center]] found unfavorable views of Israel and declining confidence in Netanyahu had risen since 2022, with opinion worsening across demographic groups and among younger voters in both major parties.[{n}] President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] publicly criticized Israeli military operations during a meeting with Netanyahu while praising [[turkey|Turkey]] as a "tremendous ally," underscoring visible policy differences even as the US-Israel alliance remained intact.[{n}]

## Badlands framing

[[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] characterized Israel as "America's greatest foreign adversary" and as an empire that in its own eyes "has only begun to tap into its true potential," arguing that when that potential is fully realized "Israel will rule the world."[{n}] He compared the Zionist State of Israel to the Sanhedrin of the ancient world, asserting that it "does not seek the glory of God, but only the glory for itself," and suggested that Trump's stated war against Israel "using Iran as his proxy" may mean reputational rather than violent conflict.[{n}]

turkey.title: Turkey
turkey.body:
## Trump's "tremendous ally" remark (2026)

Amid renewed strains between Washington and Jerusalem in July 2026, President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] praised Turkey as a "tremendous ally" while hosting Israeli Prime Minister [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]] and publicly criticizing Israeli military operations.[{n}] [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] read the praise as deliberate signaling, recalling that in September 2025 Trump invited [[recep-tayyip-erdogan|Recep Tayyip Erdogan]] to the White House the day before Netanyahu addressed the UN General Assembly, and asked what moves would be made against Turkey after Netanyahu's visit — and when Russia would finally get involved in "solving this riddle."[{n}]

recep-tayyip-erdogan.title: Recep Tayyip Erdogan
recep-tayyip-erdogan.body:
## Signaling role in US-Israel relations

[[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] argued in July 2026 that President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] repeatedly uses Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to signal his intentions toward [[israel|Israel]].[{n}] He noted that in September 2025, when Prime Minister [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]] sought to "crash the White House" during the UN General Assembly, Trump reacted by inviting Erdogan to the White House the day before Netanyahu was scheduled to address the assembly of nations; with Netanyahu again inviting himself in 2026, Trump was again elevating Erdogan and [[turkey|Turkey]], praising the country as a "tremendous ally."[{n}]
